sections.name: plannedDurationMonths
sections.title: Planned schedule length in months
sections.what: Works out how many months a project was planned to take. It uses the explicit planned duration if the project has one. Otherwise it uses the months between the construction start and the completion date, but only if both are full calendar dates.
sections.why: The comment says a bare year or a generic project start must never be treated as a construction baseline, so the function refuses to guess.
sections.watch_out: Months are averaged, so the result is approximate and may differ by a few days from a calendar count.

sections.name: scheduleOverrunPercent
sections.title: Schedule overrun percentage
sections.what: Divides the delay in months by the planned months and returns a percentage. Returns nothing if either value is missing, not a number, or the planned months are zero or negative.
sections.why: Likely reason: a percentage cannot be calculated sensibly without a valid planned length, so the function returns nothing instead of a misleading number.
sections.watch_out: A null result means unknown, not zero. Callers that treat it as zero will show a false on-time result.

summary: Calculates how many months a construction schedule was planned to take and by what percentage it overran, so on-screen and exported charts use one shared rule.
purpose: Keeps the schedule maths the same everywhere the charts appear.
why: The header comment says it is the shared convention for both on-screen and exported charts. The code refuses to guess a baseline from a bare year or a generic start date.
how: For the planned duration, it first uses the explicit planned duration if it is a positive number. Otherwise it counts the months between the construction start and the completion date, but only if both are full calendar dates. If neither works, it returns nothing. For the overrun percentage, it divides the delay in months by the planned months and multiplies by 100, returning nothing if a value is missing or the planned months are not positive.
inputs: A project with an optional schedule planned duration, a construction start date, and a completion date. For the overrun, a delay in months and a planned duration in months.
outputs: A number of months or nothing, and a percentage or nothing.
risks: Months are counted as average months of 30.4375 days, so durations are approximate. A missing result must be handled by the caller, or the chart will drop or misplace the project.
debug: If a percentage is missing, check that the project has either a planned duration or a full start and completion date in year-month-day form. If values look off, check the delay and planned months for the same project.
